# views.py - Django REST API for document approval workflow
from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated
from django.db import models, transaction
from django.conf import settings
import boto3
import time
import hashlib

class Document(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default='draft')  # draft, pending, approved
    approved_by = models.CharField(max_length=100, null=True)
    s3_key = models.CharField(max_length=500)
    approval_count = models.IntegerField(default=0)
    required_approvals = models.IntegerField(default=2)
    published_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True)


class ApproveDocumentView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]

    def post(self, request, doc_id):
        """Approve a document. When approval threshold is met, publish to S3."""
        user = request.user.username
        
        # Read current state
        doc = Document.objects.get(id=doc_id)
        
        if doc.status == 'approved':
            return Response({'error': 'Already approved'}, status=400)
        
        if doc.status != 'pending':
            return Response({'error': 'Document must be in pending state'}, status=400)
        
        # Simulate approval logic with deliberate TOCTOU window
        current_count = doc.approval_count
        new_count = current_count + 1
        
        # Non-atomic update - race condition window
        time.sleep(0.01)  # Simulates processing delay
        
        Document.objects.filter(id=doc_id).update(
            approval_count=new_count,
            approved_by=user
        )
        
        # Re-read to check threshold
        doc.refresh_from_db()
        
        if doc.approval_count >= doc.required_approvals:
            # Publish to S3 - this is the sensitive action
            self._publish_to_s3(doc, user)
            Document.objects.filter(id=doc_id).update(status='approved')
            return Response({'status': 'approved', 'published': True})
        
        return Response({'status': 'pending', 'approvals': new_count})

    def _publish_to_s3(self, doc, approver):
        """Upload approved document to the public-facing S3 bucket."""
        s3_client = boto3.client('s3',
            region_name=settings.AWS_REGION,
            endpoint_url=settings.S3_ENDPOINT_URL  # Uses VPC endpoint if configured
        )
        
        content = f"APPROVED: {doc.title}\nApproved by: {approver}\nKey: {doc.s3_key}"
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()
        
        # Upload to publication bucket
        s3_client.put_object(
            Bucket=settings.PUBLICATION_BUCKET,
            Key=f"published/{doc.s3_key}",
            Body=content.encode(),
            Metadata={
                'approver': approver,
                'content-hash': content_hash,
                'approval-count': str(doc.approval_count)
            },
            ContentType='application/pdf'
        )
        
        # Also write to audit trail bucket
        s3_client.put_object(
            Bucket=settings.AUDIT_BUCKET,
            Key=f"audit/{doc.id}/{int(time.time())}.json",
            Body=f'{{"action":"publish","user":"{approver}","doc":"{doc.id"}}'.encode(),
            ContentType='application/json'
        )


class BulkApproveView(APIView):
    """Batch approval endpoint - processes multiple docs."""
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]

    def post(self, request):
        doc_ids = request.data.get('document_ids', [])
        results = []
        for doc_id in doc_ids:
            # Each approval is independent - amplifies race window
            view = ApproveDocumentView()
            view.request = request
            resp = view.post(request, doc_id)
            results.append({'id': doc_id, 'result': resp.data})
        return Response({'results': results})

The publication bucket 'corp-published-docs' has a bucket policy allowing PutObject from the EC2 instance role. No additional network-level restrictions on S3 access. Gunicorn with 8 workers handles concurrent requests. PostgreSQL RDS with default transaction isolation (READ COMMITTED).

config.bucket_policy: Allows PutObject from instance role ARN, no condition keys
